cards.text: It's the fourth year of King Darius of Persia (Ezra 4:24), and on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Chislev, the word of the LORD comes to the prophet Zechariah. Now the people of Bethel have sent Sharezer and Regem-melech, along with their men, to plead before the LORD. And friend, they did not come for small talk.

cards.question: The men sent from Bethel have come to plead before the LORD. Who do they bring their question to?

answers.text: The elders at the city gate

cards.text: Here's their question: "Should I weep and fast in the fifth month, as I have done these many years?" That's the meeting that's been on your calendar for YEARS, and one brave soul finally asks, "Wait. Are we still doing this?"
Then the word of the LORD of Hosts comes to Zechariah, and God has some questions of His own. That's when you ask your boss a quick yes-or-no, and she says, "Come into my office."

cards.question: The LORD tells Zechariah to put His question only to the men sent from Bethel.
The people have fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months for seventy years. What does God ask them about it?

answers.text: Whether it was really for Him

cards.text: Then God asks about the eating and drinking too: weren't they doing that simply for themselves? Oof, that's a friend scrolling your gym selfies and asking, real quiet, "So... was the workout for your heart, or for the likes?"

cards.question: After His questions about fasting and eating, God asks: weren't these the words He proclaimed through the ___ who came earlier?
Back when the earlier prophets spoke, what were Jerusalem and its surrounding towns like?

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Zechariah again, and there's no riddle and no mystery this time. God spells out exactly what He's telling His people to do.

cards.question: The first thing the LORD of Hosts tells His people is to administer true justice.

cards.text: Right after that: show loving devotion and compassion to one another. Real simple, real hard.

cards.question: God says the ___ is one of the people His people must not oppress, along with the widow, the fatherless and the foreigner.

cards.text: And one more: don't plot evil in your hearts against one another. Now, how did the people take all this?

cards.question: When God's words came through the earlier prophets, the people paid close attention.

cards.text: They refused, turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped up their ears. That's me and the snooze button: the alarm is RIGHT THERE yelling, and I just roll over and pull my chef's hat down over my ears.

cards.question: God says the people made their hearts like flint. What's that picture saying?

answers.text: Their hearts were hard and unbending
Their hearts were soft and easy to shape
Their hearts were warm and wide open

cards.text: They would not listen to the law or to the words the LORD of Hosts had sent by His Spirit through the earlier prophets. Therefore great anger came from the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts says He called and the people would not listen. So what happens when they call to Him?

answers.text: He sent them a new prophet

cards.question: The LORD says He scattered the people with a whirlwind among nations they had not known.
Once the people were scattered, the land behind them was left ___ so that no one could come or go.

cards.text: They turned the pleasant land into a desolation. Hold that thought, friend, because Bethel's question about fasting is still sitting on the table.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the action in the verse. Zechariah 7:6 asks whether the eating and drinking was done simply for themselves. The joke instead weighs a workout done 'for your heart' against one done 'for the likes,' which is doing it for other people's approval. The joke also mixes two meanings of 'heart' (health and devotion). The comparison needs the same action: doing something for yourself instead of for God.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'there's no riddle and no mystery this time' adds a claim the text doesn't make. It says God's earlier word (7:4-7) was a riddle or a mystery. A storyteller line can carry the moment, but it can't describe the earlier message in a way the text doesn't support.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: 'God spells out exactly what He's telling His people to do' (and 'tells His people' on card 2) names the hearers in the present tense. In 7:9-10 the hearers aren't named. In 7:11-14, 'they' refused, the LORD scattered them, and the land was left desolate, all in the past, tied to the earlier prophets (7:12). Presenting the commands as words to the people of Zechariah's day closes a question the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Now, how did the people take all this?' follows the present-tense framing on card 1, so it reads as if the people of Zechariah's day (or Bethel's group) refused. The text shows that the ones who refused were scattered among the nations and left the land desolate (7:11-14), which is a past generation. The setup should make clear the refusal belongs to the people of the earlier prophets' day.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This asks the baker to guess the fourth item of a list. The earlier cards don't help them reason out 'poor' over 'sick,' and both are equally believable as people not to oppress. That makes it a detail guess like the Psalm 23 oil example. Give the setup more context or ask a different question, such as what the four groups have in common.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The statement depends on 'When God's words came through the earlier prophets,' which comes from 7:12 (the words sent through the earlier prophets). 7:11 alone doesn't mention the earlier prophets. The right answer (False) rests on 7:11-12, so the card should cite Zechariah 7:11-12.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.
